articles.title: The best TVs of 2026, according to experts
articles.summary: Buying a new TV? Our experts share the best TV brands, and explain the strengths and weaknesses of each.
articles.body: Shopping for the best TV can be daunting. TVs often look the same, sound the same, cost the same amount and have names that sound like a string of random numbers and letters. Learning more about TVs can be tough, too, with terms like OLED, QLED and HDR used loosely. That’s why we spoke with tech and retailer experts — to learn more about the strengths and weaknesses of each TV brand, without drowning in terminology. Narrowing in on the best brands, we selected the best TVs from each one to recommend below. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Best brand overall: Sony TV Sony is known for amazing picture quality and color accuracy, says Carl Prouty, the technologist at Abt, a national electronics and appliances retailer based in Glenview, Illinois. The brand has decades of experience creating imaging equipment for professional cinematographers and videographers, says Mark Steinberg, the senior technologist at B&H Photo & Video, a national electronics retailer in New York City. Other TV brands do not have this history, and it shows in Sony’s superior image quality, says Steinberg. Sony also has excellent built-in audio, especially in its top-end smart TVs, according to our experts. Plus, most of its TVs have Google TV built in, one of the easier interfaces to use, in my experience. Sony TVs tend to be slightly more expensive than similar models from competing brands, however. Best Sony TV: Sony Bravia 8 Series TV This isn’t Sony’s most premium consumer TV, that would be the Sony Bravia 8 II, but this model has most of the brand’s best qualities, including a vivid 4K OLED screen, fast 120Hz screen and easy-to-use Google TV software, in a fairly-priced package that’s great for most people. OLED TVs are known for rich color accuracy and contrast, which plays into Sony’s main strength: superior image quality. The Bravia 8 also has better built-in audio quality than most competitors. It projects sound from the screen itself using an advanced audio system called Acoustic Surface Audio+. This leads to much richer audio quality compared to traditional TV speakers, which occupy more limited space around the sides of the TV frame, according to our experts. Best Sony TV for brightness: Sony Bravia 7 Series TV This is a better Sony option if you plan to place it in a bright room that gets lots of natural light — the QLED screen can get much brighter than the OLED screen of the Bravia 8. It doesn’t have as rich of color and color contrast as the Bravia 8, but it still has a similarly detailed 4K resolution, fast 120Hz screen and easy-to-use Google TV software. If you want the absolute brightest Sony TV, the Sony Bravia 9 gets brighter than the Bravia 7, but it costs significantly more. Best brand for design: Samsung TV Samsung is another well-regarded brand that makes excellent TVs, some with unique designs. Its quantum dot LED (QLED) TVs are extremely bright and are a great fit for group watching in rooms that have a lot of ambient light or glare, according to our experts. Another standout from the brand is its The Frame TV, a TV with a matte finish on the screen. When turned off, it displays art and can blend into your space instead of looking like a blank void. Most Samsung TVs have the Tizen interface built in — its menus can be a little less intuitive than those on Google TV and Roku, says Steinberg (and in my experience). Best Samsung TV: Samsung QN90F Series TV This 2026 model is very bright and comes in a range of sizes that make it easy to fit in all kinds of spaces. It has advanced mini-LED lights in the panel that display a vivid, bright picture across a wide viewing angle, according to the brand. That means it’s a good fit for group daytime programming like sports. New to this version is a matte coating on the screen that reduces glare and reflections compared to previous models. Like most of the TVs on our list, it has a 4K resolution, multiple HDMI 2.1 ports, a fast refresh rate and HDR support. Best Samsung TV design: Samsung The Frame Series TV (2025) One of Samsung’s most popular TVs is The Frame Series. The screen has a matte finish that makes it less reflective than traditional screens. When turned off, it becomes a digital art frame of sorts, displaying different artwork curated by the brand. You can also upload your own images or access additional artworks from Samsung’s Art Store (for a fee). Best brand for gaming: LG TV LG TVs are great for all forms of media, but they are particularly loved by gamers, according to our experts. The brand’s OLED TVs have an especially striking, vibrant image (though image quality may not be as dynamic as Sony models, says Steinberg). The brand also has Filmmaker Mode built into its TVs: it automatically sets the picture settings to better match the TV show or movie you are watching, according to the brand. LG TV also uses the Web OS interface for its menus and control — it is relatively simple and intuitive to use (though not my absolute favorite). LG TVs are typically a little less expensive than Sony and Samsung TVs, says Steinberg. Best LG TV: LG C5 Series TV While not LG’s most high-end model (that would be the LG G5), the C5 Series is more than enough TV for most, with a striking OLED screen that has excellent color contrast and very wide viewing angles, according to the brand. Great colors, wide viewing angles, a fast screen and ample connectivity make it a good fit for movies, sports and gaming. Like most OLED TVs, the C5 is not the best fit for a bright living room — consider a Sony or Samsung QLED TV for very bright spaces that get lots of natural light. Best budget LG TV: LG B5 Series TV If the C5 Series TV is out of your budget, consider the lower-priced B5 series instead. It still has a 4K OLED panel with wide viewing angles, vivid colors and deep contrast, but is dimmer and a bit slower than the C5. You still get the same webOS smart platform, Filmmaker Mode, good gaming connectivity and compatibility with smart home devices. Best budget brand: TCL TV There are a lot of budget-friendly TV brands (Hisense, Vizio, and Insignia, to name a few), but TCL is one of the best, says Steinberg. Its TVs usually cost less than those from Sony, Samsung and LG, but still have essential features like a 4K HDR image, fast 120Hz refresh rates, modern connectivity and more. And many TCL TVs have Google TV or Roku built in, two of our favorite interfaces to use. Most TCL TVs have narrow viewing angles, meaning they do not look as good when viewed off-center. If you are looking for a TV to host a sports party, consider one of our other recommended brands. Best TCL TV: TCL QM7K Series TV TCL sells more premium models than this one (namely the QM8K), but the QM7K Series is an excellent value for the features. It has a QLED screen with mini-LEDs that deliver high brightness, vibrant colors and deep contrast, according to the brand. For gamers, it has modern HDMI 2.1 connectivity with fast refresh rates well-suited to gaming. It also has Google TV with Google Assistant built in, meaning you can control the TV with your voice. Best budget TCL TV: TCL S5 Series TV If budget is your top priority and terms like quantum dot LED, quad-OLED and local dimming zones make you want to fall asleep, the TCL S5 Series is an accessible and affordable option. It has a 4K image and an easy-to-use Google TV interface built in. It cannot compete with the image quality of our other picks, but it’s the most affordable on our list by far. It also comes in six sizes. How big should your TV be? How big your TV should be is strongly connected to how far away you’ll be watching from. Industry groups Society of Motion Picture and Television Engineers (SMPTE) and THX have formulas to calculate your optimal viewing distance and angle. Some TV manufacturers and electronics retailers (like LG and B&H Photo) recommend the same formulas, others (like TCL and Best Buy) don’t. All of them have slight differences, but ultimately give similar recommendations, averaged out below: Meet our TV experts At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Why trust NBC Selected? Harry Rabinowitz is a former reporter at NBC Selected who covered technology, fitness and deals including stories on smartwatches, running shoes, wireless earbuds and more. He covered TVs, TV brands and TV accessories for years, including stories on streaming devices, soundbars and TV mounting kits. For this piece, he spoke with television industry experts to learn more about TV brands and what makes them notable. Catch up on NBC Selected’s in-depth coverage of tech and tools, wellness and more, and follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and TikTok to stay up to date.

articles.title: Vacinas salvaram 154 milhões de vidas, mas queda na cobertura preocupa | G1
articles.standfirst: Pediatra e infectologista Sandoval Carneiro Filho alerta para o risco do retorno de doenças controladas e reforça a importância da vacinação em todas as fases da vida.
articles.summary: Pediatra e infectologista Sandoval Carneiro Filho alerta para o risco do retorno de doenças controladas e reforça a importância da vacinação em todas as fases da vida.
articles.body:
A vacinação está entre as principais responsáveis pelos avanços da saúde pública nas últimas décadas. Segundo estudo da Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS), os imunizantes salvaram 154 milhões de vidas nos últimos 50 anos, principalmente de crianças, o equivalente a seis vidas por minuto.

Reprodução — Foto: Assessoria | Unimed Cuiabá

O dado foi destacado pelo pediatra e infectologista Dr. Sandoval Carneiro Filho, cooperado da Unimed Cuiabá há 32 anos, durante entrevista ao Unicast, o podcast da Unimed Cuiabá nesta semana.

Ao lado dos antibióticos, o médico classifica as vacinas como uma das intervenções que mais impactaram a história da humanidade. O próprio sucesso da imunização, porém, criou um novo desafio: como doenças graves deixaram de fazer parte da rotina da população, também diminuiu a percepção sobre os riscos que elas representam.

“Quanto mais eficaz é a vacina, menos a doença fica visível”, explica Sandoval, ao lembrar que doenças como difteria, tétano, coqueluche, sarampo e poliomielite já foram muito mais presentes no cotidiano das famílias.

A varíola é a única doença humana completamente erradicada pela vacinação. As demais estão controladas, mas podem voltar a circular quando a cobertura vacinal cai. O especialista cita o sarampo e a coqueluche como exemplos de doenças que exigem atenção permanente.

“As gerações mais velhas viram doentes com difteria, tétano, coqueluche, sarampo e sequelas de poliomielite. Hoje, os médicos jovens que estão se formando só conhecem essas doenças nos livros e na teoria, sem ver na prática, o que dificulta até o diagnóstico caso apareça um caso. Essas doenças foram controladas pelas vacinas, mas não erradicadas. A única doença humana totalmente erradicada por vacinas foi a varíola, cujo vírus hoje existe apenas em laboratórios de alta segurança. Se baixarmos a cobertura vacinal de outras doenças, podemos ter a reemergência de surtos”, alertou Sandoval.

Apesar da alta adesão às vacinas infantis, o médico alerta que adultos e idosos frequentemente deixam de manter a caderneta atualizada. No SUS, adultos têm acesso a imunizantes contra hepatite B, difteria e tétano, febre amarela e tríplice viral.

Na rede privada, também estão disponíveis vacinas contra pneumococo e meningococo. Para pessoas acima dos 50 anos, Sandoval destaca a importância da proteção contra o herpes-zóster, que pode provocar dor intensa e comprometer a qualidade de vida.

As gestantes também precisam manter a vacinação em dia. Além de proteger a mãe, algumas vacinas permitem a transferência de anticorpos para o bebê, oferecendo proteção nos primeiros meses de vida.

Já pacientes com câncer, doenças reumatológicas, cardiopatias, diabetes, asma ou que utilizam imunossupressores podem ter acesso a imunobiológicos especiais gratuitamente pelo Centro de Referência de Imunobiológicos Especiais (CRI), mediante encaminhamento médico.

Vacina atrasada não significa começar de novo

Outra orientação importante é para quem perdeu o prazo de alguma dose. Segundo Sandoval, não é necessário reiniciar o esquema vacinal do zero. A orientação é completar as doses pendentes respeitando os intervalos mínimos recomendados.

Em caso de perda completa da carteira de vacinação e ausência de qualquer registro, o adulto deve procurar orientação profissional para avaliar a necessidade de refazer o esquema indicado para sua faixa etária.

O especialista também reforça a importância de buscar informação em fontes confiáveis, como o Ministério da Saúde, a Sociedade Brasileira de Pediatria (SBP) e a Sociedade Brasileira de Imunizações (SBIm).

Para Sandoval, manter a vacinação em dia vai além da proteção individual. Quanto maior a cobertura vacinal, menor a circulação de determinados vírus e bactérias, protegendo também pessoas que não podem receber alguns imunizantes.

O alerta ganha importância diante da retomada de casos de doenças que estavam sob controle. O médico cita a notificação recente de casos de sarampo em São Paulo como exemplo da necessidade de manter a atenção sobre a cobertura vacinal.

O desenvolvimento dos imunizantes também passa por um rigoroso processo de avaliação, que inclui estudos pré-clínicos e três fases de testes clínicos antes da liberação. Depois disso, a segurança continua sendo monitorada.

“Foi notificado recentemente o 15º caso de sarampo no estado de São Paulo. Vacinar não é uma atitude individual, é uma atitude coletiva. Prefiro o termo imunidade coletiva, em vez de "imunidade de rebanho. Quando a maioria se vacina, a circulação do vírus cai drasticamente, protegendo inclusive quem é mais vulnerável e não pode tomar a vacina”, reforçou Sandoval.

Ao falar sobre o futuro, Sandoval aponta a vacina contra o HIV como um dos grandes avanços que gostaria de ver desenvolvidos. Para ele, um imunizante capaz de prevenir a infecção representaria um marco histórico.

“A vacina contra o HIV. Embora existam tratamentos eficazes, a vacina libertaria os pacientes do uso contínuo de medicamentos e seria um marco para a humanidade”, finalizou.

articles.title: Medicina por um Dia leva estudantes do Ensino Médio a rotina médica | G1
articles.standfirst: Experiência no campus de Campinas reúne aula prática de Anatomia, contato com peças anatômicas e uma primeira vivência com a formação em Medicina.
articles.summary: Experiência no campus de Campinas reúne aula prática de Anatomia, contato com peças anatômicas e uma primeira vivência com a formação em Medicina
articles.body:
Medicina por um Dia aproxima estudantes do Ensino Médio da rotina médica na Mandic — Foto: Crédito: Divulgação.

Escolher uma carreira envolve pesquisa, planejamento e, sempre que possível, contato com a rotina da profissão. Na Faculdade São Leopoldo Mandic, estudantes do Ensino Médio podem viver essa aproximação por meio do Medicina por um Dia, iniciativa que abre as portas do campus de Campinas para uma experiência prática e orientada.

Durante a atividade, os participantes conhecem a infraestrutura acadêmica, visitam laboratórios e têm uma aula prática de Anatomia. A proposta permite que o estudante saia do campo apenas teórico e observe, de forma acompanhada, como conteúdos das ciências médicas aparecem no dia a dia da graduação.

Uma experiência para transformar curiosidade em repertório

Para Bianca, coordenadora e professora do Poliedro de Campinas, a visita é especialmente relevante porque aproxima os jovens de situações que eles já começam a discutir em sala de aula.

“É uma oportunidade deles olharem para a anatomia humana e terem uma experiência do que é a Medicina, caso optem por seguir a carreira médica ou o caminho das ciências médicas de uma forma geral”, afirma.

Na aula prática, os estudantes podem manusear peças anatômicas sob orientação e ampliar o entendimento sobre o corpo humano. A vivência também abre espaço para temas que fazem parte da formação médica desde o início, como respeito, responsabilidade e empatia no contato com o paciente.

Bianca destaca ainda a receptividade da instituição e a relação construída com as escolas participantes.

“A faculdade tem uma estrutura incrível e recebe muito bem os nossos alunos. É uma parceria muito legal, que a gente sempre fica feliz de trazer os alunos para cá. Eles também gostam muito e é um momento de muita aprendizagem”, completa.

A experiência ajuda o estudante a formular perguntas mais concretas sobre a graduação: como são as aulas práticas, quais ambientes fazem parte do curso, como funciona o aprendizado de Anatomia e de que forma a relação com pacientes e com a equipe de saúde é construída ao longo da formação.

Para quem ainda está decidindo o próximo passo após o Ensino Médio, esse contato pode funcionar como um primeiro exercício de orientação profissional. Em vez de conhecer a Medicina apenas por relatos ou conteúdos on-line, o participante vivencia parte do ambiente acadêmico e observa de perto elementos que farão parte dos seis anos de graduação.

Escolas e estudantes interessados podem consultar as informações e solicitar o agendamento da experiência no site da São Leopoldo Mandic: agende o Medicina por um Dia .

O Grupo Mandic atua em educação e saúde, com formação em Medicina e Odontologia, graduação e pós-graduação, além de atividades de pesquisa, extensão e assistência. A estrutura acadêmica reúne laboratórios, ambientes de simulação, clínicas-escola e cenários de prática em hospitais próprios e conveniados e em Unidades Básicas de Saúde.

As unidades de Medicina da São Leopoldo Mandic em Campinas, Araras e Limeira integram a proposta acadêmica do Grupo, com formação prática desde os primeiros anos e infraestrutura voltada ao desenvolvimento de competências clínicas, científicas e humanísticas.

articles.title: Jurema Águas Quentes amplia hospedagem de alto padrão no Paraná | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova hospedagem em Iretama combina privacidade, serviços personalizados, gastronomia e acesso à estrutura de lazer do complexo.
articles.summary: Nova hospedagem em Iretama combina privacidade, serviços personalizados, gastronomia e acesso à estrutura de lazer do complexo.
articles.body:
O Jurema Águas Quentes , complexo de resorts em Iretama (PR), amplia sua oferta de hospedagem com a Casa Jurema Imperial, nova opção de alto padrão que recebeu investimento de R$ 1,5 milhão. Inaugurada em agosto, a propriedade foi criada para atender hóspedes que buscam privacidade, conforto e uma experiência personalizada , mantendo o acesso à estrutura de lazer e aos serviços oferecidos pelo destino.

Localizada na área do Lagos de Jurema, a Casa Jurema Imperial funciona como uma hospedagem independente dentro do complexo. A proposta combina a exclusividade de uma casa privativa com a possibilidade de aproveitar as atrações e serviços dos dois resorts que integram o Jurema Águas Quentes.

Hospedagem privativa e experiência personalizada

A Casa Jurema Imperial conta com cinco suítes, sendo duas com banheiras imersivas, além de um quarto single, piscina privativa e espaço para fire pit. A hospedagem também oferece check-in e check-out realizados diretamente na propriedade, além de enxoval e serviços exclusivos.

O formato foi desenvolvido para proporcionar maior autonomia aos hóspedes, que podem utilizar a estrutura da casa e, ao mesmo tempo, acessar as opções de lazer do complexo de resorts em Iretama.

Gastronomia personalizada durante a estadia

A experiência de hospedagem também inclui diferentes possibilidades gastronômicas. O café da manhã é livre e pode ser realizado em qualquer um dos dois empreendimentos do Jurema Águas Quentes . Os hóspedes podem ainda escolher entre os regimes de meia pensão e pensão completa.

Outra opção é a contratação de um chef para preparar refeições personalizadas na própria Casa Jurema Imperial, ampliando as possibilidades de uma estadia mais privativa e adaptada às preferências de cada grupo.

Para Ricardo Dias, diretor de Vendas e Marketing do Jurema Águas Quentes, a nova hospedagem acompanha a busca dos viajantes por experiências mais personalizadas.

“A Casa Imperial amplia as possibilidades de hospedagem dentro do resort e foi pensada para quem deseja uma experiência mais exclusiva, com privacidade e autonomia, mas sem se afastar da estrutura que o complexo oferece. É uma proposta que une conforto, personalização e a liberdade de construir a estadia de acordo com as preferências de cada hóspede” , afirma o executivo.

articles.title: Descomplicando Carreiras: como é trabalhar com Psicologia? | G1
articles.standfirst: No segundo episódio do quadro, Pedro Gomes conversa com o psicólogo Kleison Duque sobre a profissão, as possibilidades de atuação e a Terapia Cognitivo-Comportamental.
articles.summary: No segundo episódio do quadro, Pedro Gomes conversa com o psicólogo Kleison Duque sobre a profissão, as possibilidades de atuação e a Terapia Cognitivo-Comportamental.
articles.body:
Escolher uma carreira envolve conhecer, na prática, o que está por trás de cada profissão. No segundo episódio do Descomplicando Carreiras, Pedro Gomes, conversa com o psicólogo Kleison Duque sobre a área de Psicologia e os diferentes caminhos que podem ser seguidos por quem escolhe essa profissão.

Durante o bate-papo, Kleison conta um pouco da sua experiência profissional e explica como é a atuação do psicólogo no cuidado com as emoções, os comportamentos e as relações. Entre os temas abordados está a Terapia Cognitivo-Comportamental (TCC), uma das abordagens utilizadas na área.

O episódio também ajuda a entender melhor a rotina desse profissional e as possibilidades de atuação que a Psicologia oferece, trazendo informações para quem está pensando em seguir esse caminho.

O Descomplicando Carreiras faz parte do projeto Aprova com o Sagrado , do Colégio Sagrado Coração , e apresenta diferentes profissões a partir da experiência de profissionais que compartilham suas trajetórias e os desafios do mercado de trabalho.

articles.title: Trump deve nomear Jay Clayton como 'czar' da inteligência artificial. | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a CNN, o atual diretor de inteligência dos EUA comandará força-tarefa dedicada a fomentar a tecnologia nos Estados Unidos; anúncio pode ocorrer nesta sexta-feira.
articles.summary: Segundo a CNN, o atual diretor de inteligência nacional comandará força-tarefa dedicada a fomentar a tecnologia nos Estados Unidos; anúncio pode ocorrer nesta sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Jay Clayton, diretor da inteligência dos EUA, durante reunião com executivos das empresas de IA na Casa Branca — Foto: KEVIN DIETSCH / GETTY IMAGES / VIA AFP

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , deve escolher Jay Clayton para o posto de "czar" de inteligência artificial da Casa Branca . A informação foi divulgada pela rede CNN, a partir de duas fontes familiarizadas com as discussões.

A decisão envolvendo Clayton, que hoje ocupa o cargo de diretor de inteligência nacional, pode ser oficializada pelo presidente já nesta sexta-feira (2).

A escolha do nome avança na promessa feita por Trump em setembro, quando confirmou a criação do cargo e a estruturação de uma força-tarefa voltada ao fomento da tecnologia no país .

Na ocasião, o presidente defendeu a aceleração da inteligência artificial e afirmou que o governo não vai "impedir ou sufocar o crescimento desta indústria incrível".

Trump já descartou a elaboração de leis e normas nacionais para regular o setor e chegou a classificar ações contra a inteligência artificial e os centros de dados como uma "conspiração doentia". O presidente americano defende uma autorregulação do setor de IA.

O foco do governo americano na autorregulação foi formalizado no fim de setembro . Executivos de empresas como Google, Nvidia, Anthropic e X assinaram um código de boas práticas voluntário na Casa Branca.

O documento, apresentado por Trump em uma carta de princípios de apenas uma página, estabelece diretrizes consideradas moralmente vinculativas para gerenciar riscos de segurança.

O acordo prevê quatro níveis de supervisão interna para evitar que os sistemas propaguem ameaças cibernéticas, biológicas ou químicas, além de instituir auditorias externas independentes. A medida é uma resposta a incidentes recentes do setor.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o CEO da Meta, Mark Zukerberg, durante encontro de Trump com CEOs de empresas de IA na Casa Branca, em 29 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Kevin Lamarque/ Reuters

O novo código de boas práticas também prevê a criação de um comitê independente de gestores para revisar as avaliações de segurança, iniciativa inspirada nos órgãos de autorregulação do mercado financeiro dos Estados Unidos.

O tema recebe tratamento prioritário em Washington. O governo norte-americano considera os avanços na área cruciais para a competitividade econômica e militar dos Estados Unidos, cenário acentuado pelo desacordo constante com a China em relação ao acesso a chips avançados e à dinâmica da indústria.

Ex-advogado do escritório Sullivan & Cromwell, Jay Clayton é especializado nas áreas de fusões, aquisições e captação de recursos.

Durante o primeiro mandato de Donald Trump, ele presidiu a Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (SEC). No cargo, construiu uma reputação de perfil moderado e buscou consenso com os comissários democratas.

Em abril de 2025, Trump nomeou Clayton para atuar como procurador interino do Distrito Sul de Nova York. A posição é considerada uma das promotorias mais poderosas do país.

Desde junho de 2026, Clayton ocupa o cargo de diretor de inteligência dos EUA. A posição lidera as ações de espionagem do governo norte-americano.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo em Natal: chuva nas manhãs de sábado e domingo | G1
articles.standfirst: São esperadas temperaturas entre 24°C e 29°C no fim de semana; sábado deve ter chuva pela manhã, enquanto domingo terá possibilidade de chuva também no período da manhã.
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo em Natal indica temperaturas entre 24°C e 29°C, com possibilidade de chuva nas manhãs de sábado e no domingo de votação.
articles.body:
Tempo nublado em Natal — Foto: Carmem Félix

Natal deve ter um fim de semana com sol entre nuvens e possibilidade de chuva, segundo a previsão do Climatempo. A temperatura deve ficar entre 24°C e 29°C no sábado e no domingo.

No sábado (3) , feriado estadual dos Mártires de Cunhaú e Uruaçu, a previsão indica chuva durante a manhã e diminuição das nuvens à tarde. A temperatura varia entre 24°C e 29°C, com 75% de chance de chuva e previsão de 4 mm. À noite, o céu deve ficar com muitas nuvens.

Já no domingo (4) , dia do primeiro turno das eleições, a previsão é de chuva pela manhã, seguida de redução da nebulosidade à tarde. A mínima prevista é de 24°C, e a máxima chega a 29°C. A possibilidade de chuva é de 75%, com estimativa de 4 mm.

Os ventos devem soprar de leste a sudeste ao longo do fim de semana, com velocidade em torno de 20 km/h e rajadas que podem passar de 40 km/h.

A previsão pode sofrer alterações até o fim de semana, por isso o Climatempo recomenda acompanhar as atualizações.

articles.body:
Equipes do Ministério Público do Estado do Pará, com apoio do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Repressão ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco), cumprem mandados de busca e apreensão nesta sexta-feira (2) na Prefeitura de Marabá , no sudeste paraense.

Por este motivo, ainda não há informações adicionais sobre os alvos ou o teor das investigações que possam ser divulgadas no momento.

articles.title: Neymar vira Justin Bieber em vídeo com IA ao som de rap e champanhe  | G1
articles.standfirst: Jogador do Santos aparece cercado por seguranças e pessoas dançando enquanto aparenta dublar “Pop Star”.
articles.summary: Jogador do Santos aparece cercado por seguranças e pessoas dançando enquanto aparenta dublar “Pop Star”.
articles.body:
Neymar vira 'Lil Ney' em vídeo com IA ao som de rap e champanhe — Foto: Redes Sociais

Neymar Jr. publicou nas redes sociais um vídeo feito com inteligência artificial (IA) em que aparece recriando cenas do clipe de 'Pop Star', de Justin Bieber. A montagem coloca a imagem do jogador do Santos sobre a do cantor, repetindo movimentos e gestos enquanto ele aparenta dublar a música.

Nas imagens, Neymar surge descendo as escadas de uma casa, segurando uma garrafa de champanhe e acompanhado por um segurança. Depois, passa por diferentes ambientes do imóvel, que está cheio de pessoas dançando. A publicação já ultrapassou 200 mil visualizações no Instagram.

A aparência de Neymar no vídeo também foi construída a partir de uma imagem do jogador durante a Copa do Mundo. Ele aparece com o agasalho da Seleção Brasileira e um colete rosa de reserva.

Na imagem original, a peça tinha uma estampa com o número 26 e uma taça vazada, em referência ao ano da competição. Na versão criada por IA, o desenho foi reinterpretado e aparece como um zero na parte da frente e um cinco nas costas.

Na legenda, o atacante escreveu apenas "Lil Ney". O termo "Lil" é comum entre artistas do rap e do hip-hop e aparece no nome artístico de rappers como Lil Wayne, Lil Baby e Lil Uzi Vert.

Nos comentários, a brincadeira também rendeu comparações com outros artistas. Um internauta chamou o camisa 10 de "Ney Bieber".

articles.summary: A US Energy Department electrical engineer has been arrested for allegedly providing material support to Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, including by
articles.body: A US Energy Department electrical engineer has been arrested for allegedly providing material support to Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels, including by purchasing materials used in homemade explosives and drones and traveling to Yemen, the Justice Department said.Ashton Hamed Ellaboudy, 51, of Richland, Washington, was arrested Thursday and is scheduled to make his first court appearance Friday, the Associated Press reported, citing the Justice Department. Court records did not list an attorney who could speak on his behalf.According to the FBI, Ellaboudy sought to help the Houthis improve their communications capabilities and traveled to Yemen in September last year. He allegedly used a passport issued while he was working with the US Army Corps of Engineers to travel to Oman before entering Yemen.After returning to the US, Ellaboudy allegedly told Customs and Border Protection officials that he had been in Oman on a work trip and was part of a US government mission inspecting missile defence systems.His supervisor, however, told investigators he was unaware of Ellaboudy making any international trip or of any Energy Department missile inspection programme involving him, according to an FBI affidavit.Investigators began looking into Ellaboudy after learning that he had purchased precursor chemicals, including acetone and sodium bisulfate, that can be used in homemade explosives, as well as components used in drones, the FBI said.He also allegedly communicated with several FBI informants, including one posing as a Houthi colonel, and offered advice and assistance involving communications equipment.Ellaboudy allegedly told informants that he had been smuggled into and out of Yemen and wanted to reach the capital, Sanaa, to establish government-level contacts. He was ultimately unable to reach the city, according to the FBI.Ellaboudy has been charged under a US law that prohibits providing material support to organisations designated as foreign terrorist organisations. The Houthis are designated as such by the US.If convicted, Ellaboudy could face up to 20 years in prison, according to the Justice Department.The Houthis seized control of Sanaa and parts of Yemen in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led military intervention the following year in support of the country's internationally recognised government. articles.title: Ukraine calls for tighter sanctions as Russian attacks spark Kyiv gridlock
articles.summary: Closure of bridges struck by drones in Ukrainian capital causes traffic chaos.
articles.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called on allies to tighten sanctions against Russia after a wave of strikes triggered gridlock across Kyiv.

Traffic chaos gripped the Ukrainian capital on Friday after Russian drone attacks overnight closed key bridges. Zelenskyy called for allies to act to prevent Moscow from sourcing components for its arsenal as Kyiv and other parts of Ukraine face attacks around the clock.

Kyiv’s Southern Bridge and Paton Bridge, key routes for cars and public transport across the Dnipro River, were closed in both directions after the attacks. The Metro Bridge was closed in the direction of Kyiv’s right bank, the city administration said.

Zelenskyy wrote in a social media post that Iranian-type Shahed kamikaze drones struck the Southern Bridge “several times”. One person was killed as Russia launched more than 100 drones across the country.

Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko later said Russian aerial attacks forced the partial closure of three bridges over the Dnipro River.

He said Russia was “tearing Kyiv apart” and that the city should now be on a war footing.

“The capital is in a very dramatic situation,” Klitschko posted on Telegram. “It’s no longer possible to pretend that we can live now as we lived in peacetime.”

Long lines of stationary cars and buses were gridlocked on main roads as commuters sought alternative routes or made their way on foot.

“I’ve been travelling for three hours … to get to work,” Tetiana Osypenko, a 49-year-old seamstress whose bus was stuck in a traffic jam, told the AFP news agency. “There’s just no way to get there. Nothing. It’s impossible to cross the bridges today.”

Zelenskyy, who has persistently called for additional help to boost Ukraine’s air defences during Moscow’s concentrated air campaign , noted that supply chains for such weapons trail through Europe, the United States, China and Japan.

“No matter how hard Moscow tries to fully localise the production of its drones and missiles, its ability to escalate remains critically dependent on foreign components,” Zelenskyy wrote. “Most of these companies are well-known manufacturers, but their components still make their way to Russia.”

“Every Russian drone can actually be stopped right at the production line. What is needed is the political will of these countries,” he continued. “If the Kremlin has chosen more strikes, sanctions must work and must be strengthened.”

Last month, European Union foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas said the bloc was “working on new proposals to tighten sanctions enforcement” and implement new measures.

US President Donald Trump separately signed a sweeping Russian sanctions package into law, taking aim at Russian President Vladimir Putin, banks, other financial institutions, and the energy and defence sectors.

Elsewhere in Ukraine on Friday, Russian strikes targeted a kindergarten in Kherson, a grocery store in Kharkiv and apartment buildings in Kramatorsk and Sumy, Zelenskyy said.

The Dnipro, Odesa, Kharkiv, Kyiv, Poltava and Rivne regions also came under attack with at least four people reported wounded.

The Russian Ministry of Defence said on Telegram that its drones hit a bridge over the Dnipro River in Kyiv, a power station in the surrounding region, the Izmail port near Odesa and a cargo vessel. It claimed all the sites were used for Ukrainian military purposes.

Ukraine’s military carried out its own overnight attacks on Russia and said they hit a Lukoil facility in the city of Volgograd as well as an oil dispatch station in the Samara region with fires breaking out at both sites.

Ukrainian forces also carried out missions in several other Russian regions that targeted airfields, industrial sites and other facilities, including in the Black Sea, Zelenskyy said.

Russian authorities in the Black Sea port town of Tuapse said an enterprise was damaged by drone debris, but they did not provide details.

articles.title: 'May Bapu’s timeless message keep guiding us': PM Modi pays tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, attends prayer meet
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday attended a special interfaith prayer meeting at Gandhi Smriti in New Delhi on the occasion of Mahatma
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday attended a special interfaith prayer meeting at Gandhi Smriti in New Delhi on the occasion of Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary, where he paid floral tributes to the Father of the Nation.Earlier in the day, PM Modi paid floral tributes to Gandhi at Rajghat and former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri at Vijay Ghat to mark their respective birth anniversaries. In a post on X, the Prime Minister had further said the lives of Gandhi and Shastri, marked by “simplicity, courage and service to the nation”, continue to inspire generations. He said their ideals and commitment to India's progress would remain a guiding light.PM had earlier paid tribute to Gandhi on his 157th birth anniversary and called for greater adoption of Swadeshi, with Khadi at the forefront. He urged people to buy at least one Khadi product on October 2 and take pride in calling it Swadeshi.“May Bapu’s timeless message keep guiding us towards a better society and a Viksit Bharat,” he said.Several other leaders also paid tribute to Gandhi and Shastri in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Union ministers JP Nadda and Kiren Rijiju, Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi were among those present.Meanwhile, school students and artists performed devotional bhajans during the prayer meeting. Vice President CP Radhakrishnan also attended the programme and paid floral tributes to Gandhi, remembering his role in India's freedom movement and his message of harmony and social upliftment.Gandhi was born on October 2, 1869, in Porbandar, Gujarat. His birth anniversary is observed as Gandhi Jayanti, while the United Nations observes October 2 as the International Day of Non-Violence.Shastri was born on October 2, 1904, in Mughalsarai, Uttar Pradesh, and served as prime minister from 1964 to 1966. articles.title: Silicon Valley investor AJ Scaramucci quietly built a collection of comics, trading cards and dinosaur fossils; now he sees them as alternative assets
articles.summary: For years, Silicon Valley investor AJ Scaramucci quietly assembled an unusual collection of comics, trading cards and even dinosaur bones.
articles.body: For years, Silicon Valley investor AJ Scaramucci quietly assembled an unusual collection of comics, trading cards and even dinosaur bones. Now he argues these objects belong alongside gold and bitcoin as serious alternative assets. Scaramucci founded Solari Capital, a venture firm that has just emerged from stealth after deploying roughly 350 million dollars, and he launched a collectables holding company called Treasure Trove earlier this year. He reasons that scarce cultural treasures can protect wealth when currencies lose value. This article explains the collection, the investment logic behind it, and how it connects to his wider technology investment thesis.Who is AJ Scaramucci, the Solari Capital founder with 350 million dollars investedScaramucci began in science, with an early interest in amateur astronomy and time in a bioelectronics laboratory, before moving to the Bay Area, joining Tesla in 2013 and then spending a rotation at Google. According to Fortune, he credits Peter Diamandis's book Abundance with shaping his worldview, and he later worked under Diamandis as an entrepreneur-in-residence and at Kai-Fu Lee's Sinovation Ventures.Solari Capital is the result. According to the report, it has put roughly 350 million dollars into early-stage investing, late-stage growth cheques and companies it incubates itself. Backers include Ron Conway, Jim Breyer, Stephen Pagliuca, Eric Schmidt and Diamandis.His company is buying grail comics and record-setting Pokémon cardsThe collection now has a corporate home. Treasure Trove, launched earlier this year, has bought a first-appearance Iron Man comic for 2 million dollars and, separately, a record-setting Pokémon card. Scaramucci says he has been buying one-of-one "grail" assets, meaning unique items that cannot be replicated, because he believes they deliver uncorrelated returns.His stated ambition is to open the market to ordinary investors, and not only the ultrawealthy. He calls collectables a sleeping giant that institutional capital has largely ignored, and he claims the category is worth 25 trillion dollars and has never been properly institutionalised. That figure is his own claim, not an independently verified number.Why collectables, trading cards and dinosaur fossils are a hedgeThe logic starts with money. Scaramucci notes that gold and bitcoin together have created more market value since 2008 than the group of seven giant technology stocks known as the Magnificent Seven. He argues that currency debasement, the steady loss of purchasing power, is a defining feature of twenty-first-century finance, and he puts the average life expectancy of a currency at around twenty-six years.In his framing, gold is the physical store of value and bitcoin the digital one, while collectables are what he calls a "cultural store of value." He describes buying them as a debasement trade, a bet that scarce objects hold their worth as currencies erode.How the shortage of Tyrannosaurus rex fossils caught his attentionAs per Fortune, Dinosaur fossils are the most unusual piece. Andrea Pasinetti, founder of the education company Kira Learning and a Solari portfolio founder, recalled that around a year and a half to two years ago Scaramucci was already talking about the short supply of Tyrannosaurus rex fossils. A few months before the report, Sotheby's sold the most expensive Tyrannosaurus rex fossil ever transacted, and Pasinetti said Scaramucci had been discussing that very specimen long before.Scaramucci presents collectables as the flip side of his main thesis, which he calls Programmable Reality. That idea holds that as computing power compounds, biology, intelligence, matter and money become things that can be engineered with software-like precision. Solari's portfolio is organised around four themes, programmable intelligence, biology, matter and finance.One trade, he says, is the artificial intelligence or singularity trade, where computing power keeps doubling. The other is the scarcity trade, or cultural trade. In his view, the two sit side by side, one bets on abundance created by technology, the other on things that cannot be made again.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Protests shutter hundreds of French schools as violence flares
articles.summary: Education minister declares students ‘in danger’ as hundreds of injuries reported across the country.
articles.body:
Hundreds of schools have been closed across France amid a student protest movement that has turned increasingly tumultuous.

At least 400 of France’s 3,700 high schools were closed on Friday, the Ministry of National Education said, with 560 reporting protests or disruptions. The demonstrations began at high schools in the Paris area last week, but they have spread nationwide and led to violent clashes with police.

On Friday, students across the country, many clad in masks, blockaded schools, lit fires in the streets, and faced off with police as they rallied against large class sizes and absent teachers .

“We are 35 per class, we don’t have enough chairs in classrooms, the one-hour lunch break [is too short] for everyone to get food,” 15-year-old Kesia told the Reuters news agency in the Paris suburb of Pantin before running off as the police used tear gas.

Fire damaged the entrances of two high schools in the capital, Leonard de Vinci in the south of the city and Gaston-Bachelard in the southeast, with the fire brigade called to extinguish the blazes.

Students waved placards reading “We have a future to build, not to endure.”

The school protest movement coincides with a public sector strike against the government’s budget plans, raising the pressure on President Emmanuel Macron before elections next year.

Approximately 2,000 people have been detained so far, the vast majority of whom are children, according to Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin.

Parents should be liable for damage caused by their children and “pay for repairs”, he told RTL.

Education Minister Edouard Geffray warned parents to “tell their children not to go” to the protests.

At least 170 students have been wounded, along with 65 school staff members, including 40 principals, he told BFMTV. More than 100 high schools have sustained “severe damage”.

“What matters now is ensuring our children are no longer out on the streets, because they are in danger,” Geffray declared.

Rights group Amnesty International wrote on social media that “the images of high school students being assaulted by law enforcement are extremely alarming”.

“Many are minors, children,” the organisation said. “They must be protected, not beaten with batons.”

Lola, a 16-year-old speaking to the AFP news agency in the western city of Rennes, condemned what she described as police violence while standing outside Jean-Mace high school.

“It makes us even angrier – the police have no right to hit us or use tear gas on us,” Lola said.

The government has accused the hard-left France Unbowed (LFI) party of commandeering the movement. Senior LFI official Manuel Bompard dismissed the assertion as a “conspiracy theory”.

In an effort to quell tensions, Geffray said he planned to meet on Friday with education unions and student associations to find room for dialogue.

articles.title: Wolf encounter: A photographer on what humans have lost
articles.summary: How a brush with the wild can expose what modern life no longer asks of us.
articles.body:
What’s the one thing people should know? Modern life has reduced how often we are truly required to meet the world on its own terms — until we encounter something that refuses to adapt to us.

It lasted only a few minutes, but Norwegian wildlife photographer Lasse Huldt Pedersen remembers his closest encounter with a wolf in meticulous detail.

Wolves usually smell humans long before they see them, but on a late summer day in 2022, Pedersen believes the wind carried his scent away from the apex predator, allowing them to come nearly face-to-face.

As he stood quietly among the pine trees in eastern Norway near the Swedish border, patiently waiting to spot a wolf, one appeared on a rocky rise above him.

The animal scanned the forest, turning its head several times before it finally sensed him. When the wolf locked onto Pedersen, it held firm eye contact, deliberately lowering its head while standing tall on the rocky outcrop — a typical feature in Scandinavia due to Ice Age glacial erosion.

The animal towered over Pedersen, who stood barefoot on the mossy, lichen-covered forest floor below — a summer habit he kept when walking in nature.

Pedersen, who has tracked wolves for years, said the sustained eye contact — with bright blue eyes he described as strikingly human — triggered a physical reaction in him. His adrenaline surged, and his heart raced. His breathing, rapid at first, slowed after several seconds, syncing with the animal’s steady breaths.

Meanwhile, the wolf stared at the bearded photographer, assessing him with calm, measured breaths.

Pedersen knew wolves rarely attack humans, but he was still hyperaware in that moment; the noise of everyday life — stress, concerns, distractions — quickly fell away.

“Nothing is more primal than staring into the eyes of a wild animal, especially the wolf,” Pedersen said.

As a photographer, he was eager to capture the moment. But Pedersen had recently broken his tripod, so he had to hold up his camera and heavy telephoto lens by hand. Adrenaline kept him nearly motionless, but as he shifted his weight, a twig snapped beneath his feet.

“Nothing is more primal than staring into the eyes of a wild animal, especially the wolf.” by Lasse Huldt Pedersen

“Nothing is more primal than staring into the eyes of a wild animal, especially the wolf.”

The wolf reacted to the noise — and for the first time appeared uncomfortable and growled briefly, possibly to signal danger to nearby wolves. Pedersen stayed as still as he could, focused on keeping the lens pointed at the wolf.

Soon, he realised the encounter was ending. The wolf let out another short growl, sniffed the air, and disappeared behind the pine trees within a second, its tail slightly curved, suggesting unease.

Pedersen marvelled at the wolf’s control over its body, moving with smooth, feline grace as it left.

“A wolf in many ways acts like a dog but moves like a cat,” he said.

articles.title: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul says Jane Doe in Cornell case was ‘failed’ by the system
articles.summary: Hochul tapped New York Attorney General Letitia James to take over the case on Thursday, as questions swirl over how local officials handled the matter.
articles.body: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul said Friday she believes the former Cornell University student who alleges she was gang raped by fraternity members in 2024 was “failed by people and institutions with an obligation to protect her,” including a county prosecutor. “I will not allow anyone to sweep this case under the rug,” Hochul told reporters at a Friday morning news conference in New York City. Hochul, reading from prepared remarks, confirmed that she has appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to carry out a “fresh and thorough review” of all the facts in the case nearly two years after a district attorney declined to pursue criminal charges. “We will review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses and, if warranted, pursue prosecutions,” James said at the news conference. “I know that you want answers. I do, too.” Hochul said she believes Cornell University did not provide enough information about the accuser’s account of the alleged sexual assault at the Chi Phi fraternity house in October 2024. Hochul also faulted Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten for not doing a more comprehensive investigation. “In what world does the district attorney not even interview her or anyone else involved, or even request the full transcript” of Jane Doe’s interview with Cornell University campus police, Hochul said. “This woman, this young woman, had already endured something that is utterly unspeakable,” Hochul added. In a statement after Hochul’s news conference, Van Houten said he supported James’ appointment, adding: “I trust that she will examine the facts and apply the law. “It has become clear that we were not provided the full picture by the University,” Van Houten said. “The focus has been and should continue to be on the victims. My office will cooperate fully with the Attorney General.” Hochul said she backs proposed changes to current New York state law, which makes it difficult for a person who has voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs to seek criminal justice for an alleged sexual assault. “Voluntary intoxication is not a license for sexual assault or gang rape. Period,” Hochul told reporters. “I support closing this loophole, and will work with the New York state Legislature to accomplish this.” The accuser, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, reported the alleged assault to university police in November 2024, about three weeks after she said it took place, according to a civil lawsuit. The Ivy League university then sent a sworn statement to Van Houten’s office. Van Houten’s office “determined the alleged facts as set forth in the statement do not constitute a crime,” the district attorney has said. In a lengthy statement Monday, Van Houten said the sworn statement Jane Doe provided to campus police “did not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang raped.” But news reports have since complicated that characterization. CBS News New York, citing a transcript of a conversation between Jane Doe and investigators, reported Wednesday that she told campus police: “I can say with 100% confidence I was raped. NBC News has not independently verified the transcript. Jane Doe’s lawsuit names seven fraternity members as defendants. It also accuses the fraternity, her sorority and a bar she visited on the night of the alleged assault of negligence. The national Chi Phi organization has called the sexual assault allegations at Cornell University “deeply concerning,” and the sorority said it could not comment on pending litigation. The bar denied serving alcohol to Jane Doe, who was under the legal drinking age at the time. Cornell has defended its 2024 investigation. In response to a request for comment on Hochul’s news conference, a Cornell spokesperson said: “We fully support the appointment of a special prosecutor and efforts to change New York State’s rape law and are committed to an independent external review of all aspects of how Cornell has handled this case.” The case has drawn extensive news coverage and wide attention on social media. Hollywood celebrities such as Oscar-nominated actor Florence Pugh and “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” star Mariska Hargitay highlighted Jane Doe’s lawsuit on Instagram. “This is a human issue, not a women’s issue,” Pugh wrote in an Instagram post Sunday. “We are all involved.” If you or someone you know has been sexually assaulted, call the National Sexual Assault Hotline at 1-800-656-4673. articles.title: Illinois farmer John Dollinger's family hosted 10 wind turbines across 800 acres; payments began at $10,000 per turbine a year and, by 2025, had risen to about $120,000 annually across the farm
articles.summary: In Grundy County, Illinois, grain farmer John Dollinger gets yearly payments from ten wind turbines spread across his family's 800-acre property.
articles.body: In Grundy County, Illinois, grain farmer John Dollinger gets yearly payments from ten wind turbines spread across his family's 800-acre property. About a decade ago, the deal guaranteed him $10,000 per turbine each year. That amount has slowly increased with inflation. By 2025, each turbine paid about $12,000, giving the farm roughly $120,000 in total income each year. Dollinger's experience is part of a wider trend across rural America. According to agricultural media outlet Ambrook, more than 90 per cent of land-based wind turbines in the United States are located on private farmland. Data from the United States Department of Agriculture shows that from 2012 to 2017, 94 per cent of farmland with turbines remained in primary agricultural use. The extra income can help farmers deal with changing crop prices. But the growth of wind power continues to divide farming communities.Steady income versus land preservationFor many farmers, payments from turbine leases provide a rare source of financial security. A USDA report that studied wind energy costs from 2011 to 2020 found that farmers hosting turbines earn between $8,000 and $33,000 per turbine each year. Clayton Rosenberger farms 1,100 acres in McLean County, Illinois. He hosts one 499-foot turbine that EDP Renewables installed four years ago. The turbine, including its concrete base and access roads, takes up about two-thirds of a football field. It uses just 0.1 per cent of his total acreage. "I'm a self-employed farmer. I don't have a 401-K," Rosenberger told Ambrook. "I don't have a retirement plan, but now I do." Turbine payments can also bring more money to local governments through property taxes. Rosenberger said his township, which has 300 residents, once had trouble balancing its budget. Tax money from the wind project has since helped pay for repaved roads and new fire trucks. Still, some farmers strongly oppose turbines because they fear losing productive farmland forever. Randy Scilacci, an alfalfa grower in Pershing County, Nevada, turned down a proposal to build solar installations on his land. He said he would also reject wind turbines. Scilacci told Ambrook he was worried about heavy equipment, gravel roads and concrete foundations taking away usable soil. "You've only got so much farm ground, and there's 1% of the population that feeds the rest of the country, and you go taking that stuff out, then you're putting more pressure on the farmers that are farming to do more," Scilacci said.Operational risks and local frictionBuilding huge turbines can create practical problems for working farms. Building the bases means moving heavy equipment across fields. This can pack down fragile topsoil and damage underground tile drainage systems that are important for managing fields. There are physical dangers as well. Lightning strikes or mechanical failures can sometimes start turbine fires. Burning debris can then fall across crop rows. Even so, developers usually include payment terms in standard lease contracts. These terms compensate landowners for crop damage, soil repairs and disruption to farm operations. Insurance can also cause confusion. Oklahoma Insurance Commissioner Glen Mulready said at a Lincoln County community meeting that rural residents often wrongly believe that hosting a turbine or living near one could put their property insurance at risk. "There may be reasons you want to oppose a wind farm here in your county or in your area, but insurance isn't one of them," Mulready stated. He explained that state laws, including Oklahoma's 2011 statute, require energy companies to name host landowners directly on corporate liability policies. Community relationships can become difficult even when landowners want to sign leases. Sarah Mills, an associate professor of practice at the University of Michigan who studies wind energy adoption, found that conflict between neighbors can grow when some host turbines and others do not.Mills noted that today's wind farms use taller turbines that can produce more power. Because fewer turbines are needed to produce the same amount of electricity, fewer landowners get lease payments. At the same time, the taller turbines can be seen from a larger area. "I think this kind of lease model not evolving, is creating more haves versus have nots," Mills told Ambrook. She added that farmers who receive turbine payments often keep quiet about the money in their communities to avoid resentment from neighbors. In some places, local opposition stops wind projects altogether. In Rush County, Indiana, farmer Michael Dora signed a wind lease nearly seven years ago. But public protests over drainage problems and changes to local views led officials to place a moratorium on development. The project was eventually abandoned.Political headwinds and community alternativesThe expansion of wind power faces changing political pressures. Tax credits in the Inflation Reduction Act gave financial support to renewable energy projects. But political opposition to those subsidies could change the financial picture for developers. Julia McPherson, community relations manager at EDP Renewables, told Ambrook that renewable energy development has become more politically divided in recent years. At the same time, projects in some regions continue to bring tax money into rural government budgets. In places where farms are smaller, some farming communities have tried a shared approach to avoid creating divisions between neighbors. In Isabella County, Michigan, small farm owners worked together to create a community wind agreement that began operating in 2021. Under the agreement, every participating acre gets the same payment, whether or not a turbine is located on that particular piece of land. The agreement also includes profit-sharing if the turbines produce more energy than expected. For farmers like Rosenberger, early doubts changed after he looked at the financial deal and visited a working turbine to hear its noise for himself. "It's a good thing all the way around. I know some people probably don't like it, but they've gotten used to it," Rosenberger said. "I think because you just don't hear any rumblings in the neighborhood about them."You use AI every day. articles.title: Can India’s ‘cockroach’ movement oust Modi’s election chief?
articles.summary: India’s youth protests return to streets, eyeing PM Modi’s prized bureaucrat who oversees the world’s biggest elections.
articles.body:
New Delhi, India – Central parts of the Indian capital turned into a ghost town on Friday as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s police detained hundreds of protesters, as the ‘cockroach’ movement that ousted the country’s education minister this past summer joined opposition parties in demanding the resignation of India’s elections chief.

The government shut down metro stations leading to central Delhi and suspended internet services. Heavily deployed government forces blocked all entries to Parliament Street and the Jantar Mantar protest strip – the stage of the youth movement that forced out Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan just two months ago.

Saurav Yadav, a 24-year-old musician from Gwalior, a city in central India nearly 335km (210 miles) from New Delhi, took an overnight bus to join the protest, called by the cockroach movement and joined by a spectrum of opposition parties and unions.

But as Yadav approached the site – his first time in the Indian capital – he was dragged away by two policemen, even as he held the tricolour national flag in his hands. “This government is managing the elections. Just imagine, the only thing that gives them power is managed!” Yadav told Al Jazeera, sitting startled in the back of a police van.

“We are just cosplaying democracy,” he said, sweating profusely. “We cannot keep pretending this.”

The cockroach movement is taking the street protests to several Indian cities in the coming days, including in the country’s financial capital, Mumbai, later on Friday. But youth protest leaders, emboldened by their success against the education minister, face a new set of challenges as they set their sights on the Modi government’s most politically prized bureaucrat.

Last week, India was shaken by new revelations showing divisions within the supposedly autonomous body that is in charge of conducting its elections over controversial policies that critics say have disenfranchised tens of millions of people.

India’s Election Commission chief, Gyanesh Kumar, frequently overruled concerns raised by the two other election commissioners about the integrity of ongoing changes in the voter database, an investigation by the Indian Express reported.

The commission has not refuted the investigation, but indicated, since the revelations, that it was acting to address concerns raised by the other two election commissioners.

The revelations came after a months-long struggle by India’s opposition parties to bring what they have described as the “sabotaging” conduct of the election commission to the fore, which they say is dictated by Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for its electoral benefit.

Since June last year, the commission has been revising and updating the voters list statewide. It has struck off more than 130 million names during the exercise since then, which the critics say targeted economically weaker sections, minorities and other vulnerable groups in Indian society disproportionately.

The cockroach movement leaders moved fast to tap into the growing calls for Kumar’s resignation, terming it the “last call to save democracy”.

The leader of the opposition, Rahul Gandhi, has called for the election chief to be tried for treason against India.

N Sai Balaji, a senior leader of All India Students’ Association (AISA), the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist-Leninist) Liberation that was at the centre of youth protests earlier this year, said that “people have been suspecting the election commission for a long time – and different people have been flagging a range of issues”.

“We do not need to build a movement this time. We just need to come out on the streets, and there will be no opposition to the central demand: Gyanesh Kumar needs to go,” Balaji told Al Jazeera.

The success of the youth protests that ousted the education minister was credited to the unifying platform of education in India’s otherwise deeply divided society. “Then this is perhaps the most secular issue in India,” said Balaji. “Who is a bureaucrat to decide who gets to vote and who doesn’t?”

Balaji said that there is “a unanimous understanding across the opposition’s spectrum that the elections are managed and staged.” If Kumar stays as the chief, he said, “no one will trust any electoral outcome in the so-called world’s largest democracy.”

Kumar, India’s 62-year-old election chief, is a trusted lieutenant of PM Modi, and his career has intersected with several of the government’s most consequential and controversial decisions.

Currently, Kumar is spearheading the highly contested revision of the voters’ list.

In 2016, he was tapped as a joint secretary in the Home Ministry’s Kashmir division, which oversees the Indian-administered Kashmir. Three years later, Kumar was entrusted with drafting the legislation that sliced the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two federally controlled territories, stripping the contested region of special rights in August 2019, as the Modi government clamped down on the region with a months-long curfew and a communication blackout.

Within a few months, Kumar was moved to the Modi government’s next flagship project: the construction of a controversial Ram Temple.

On December 6, 1992, a far-right Hindu mob tore down the 16th-century Babri Mosque, triggering religious riots across the country that killed over 2,000 people, mostly Muslims. After years of legal battles, the top court awarded the site to Hindus. Kumar led the team overseeing implementation of the Supreme Court’s verdict, including the formation of a trust tasked with managing the new temple that has now come up at the site.

“Gyanesh Kumar has been the bureaucrat of choice to get these things done for the ruling government. If he is forced out, it is going to be a much bigger blow for the Modi government,” said Neelanjan Sircar, a senior fellow at the Centre for Policy Research, a think tank in New Delhi.

“The cost of losing Kumar would be higher: it would be a much bigger signal to the larger ecosystem if you can’t protect a man like that,” Sircar added.

Asim Ali, a political analyst in New Delhi, said he doesn’t expect the government to cave in. “Kumar’s resignation would be seen as a fatal admission of guilt, and it would undermine the legitimacy of elections, and hence their power,” he told Al Jazeera.

Taking a jibe at Kumar, India’s opposition leader Gandhi called on him to become a state witness, saying PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah would eventually face prosecution for “treason”.

The swift crackdown on protesters on Friday suggests the Modi government will not let the protest movement take charge of Jantar Mantar this time around, say analysts.

“Lessons that the government learned from earlier youth protests are in terms of strategy,” said Sircar, adding that the Modi government would want to avoid a confrontation with protesters. “They do not want any visuals like the last time. The goal will be to prevent any kind of assembly from an earlier stage.”

On July 20, the cockroach movement staged a sit-in at Jantar Mantar, then called on thousands of protesters to march peacefully towards Parliament. They were met with police brutality, leaving more than 100 students injured.

The visuals then galvanised a wider Gen Z uprising in the national capital, with protesters choking key streets in central Delhi, and eventually forcing the removal of the education minister.

But Ali, the political analyst warned that the protest leaders are more experienced now. The cockroach movement, which grew into the Gen Z uprising, was born out of a casual joke on X after the chief justice of India equated unemployed youth to “cockroaches”.

None of the central leaders had experience of organising a mass movement at the time. Now, they are returning to the streets “as experienced protest leaders, who have developed a following.”

“There are no assured brakes,” Ali said. “And that makes this situation more explosive.”

articles.title: Ken Urker, partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, found dead in Louisiana home
articles.summary: Ken Urker, the partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, made comments about being depressed before being found dead in his Louisiana home from an apparent drug overdose, authorities said.
articles.body: Ken Urker, the partner of Gypsy Rose Blanchard, made comments about being depressed before being found dead in his Louisiana home from an apparent drug overdose, authorities said. Deputies responded to a home in Raceland around 6:15 p.m. Thursday and found Urker dead, the Lafourche Sheriff’s Office said in a statement. “At this time, we are continuing the death investigation,” the office said. The sheriff’s office said in an emailed statement that it found no evidence of foul play. An initial report released by the sheriff’s office states that officers were called to Urker’s home for a wellness check. A man and Urker’s boss gained access to the home through an unlocked window and found him lying on his bed, cold to the touch, the report says. Deputies searching the home found paraphernalia, including syringes and a spoon, in a bathroom next to a “brown powdery substance,” according to the report. A syringe, a holstered handgun and two shot glasses were on the nightstand next to the bed, the report says. Authorities noted it appeared that Urker had been there “for an extended period of time.” The man who found Urker told deputies that he and his wife had attended church with Urker on Wednesday night and that Urker had made comments about being depressed and upset, according to the report. The report states that Urker had also made a TikTok video of him driving without saying anything. The man said they decided to check on Urker because of his behavior and because he failed to show up to work. The cause of death has not been revealed. Blanchard, who welcomed a daughter with Urker in 2024, told People magazine that Urker had overdosed and she was in “disbelief.” The magazine reported that he died on his 34th birthday. “I can’t think,” she said. “I’ve screamed until my throat burns.” The couple met through a pen pal program while Blanchard was in prison for her role in the 2015 murder of her mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard, Variety reported. The pair briefly split and then reconciled in 2024. Blanchard has said her mother abused her for years and forced her to fake serious illnesses. She pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and was sentenced to 10 years in prison. Her then-boyfriend, Nicholas Godejohn, was sentenced to life in prison for fatally stabbing Dee Dee Blanchard. The killing sparked a media frenzy and inspired HBO’s 2017 documentary “Mommy Dead and Dearest” and the 2019 Hulu series “The Act.” Blanchard was released early in 2023 after being granted parole. She told People that Urker was heavily scrutinized during their relationship. “Ken endured an unimaginable level of public scrutiny and relentless cyberbullying across social media platforms, including TikTok and Reddit. The cruelty directed toward him was something no human being should have to endure,” she said in her statement. “I believe the tremendous weight of that scrutiny and harassment had a profound impact on him, and I hope his passing serves as a reminder that there is a real person behind every screen, every headline, and every comment.” Blanchard also said she wants their daughter to grow up “knowing how deeply her father loved her and who he was beyond what strangers on the internet chose to say about him.” The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration has a 24/7 National Helpline for individuals with substance abuse issues and their family members. The hotline, which offers assistance in English and Spanish, can be reached at 1-800-662-HELP (4357). To find behavioral health treatment services, visit SAMHSA’s website.
