Zilis made the statement reacting to a post that noticed that Elon Musk was not following Zilis on X anymore. "It’s hard to go from in love to let go in a week with no warning, but that’s just how it is sometimes," Zilis wrote.Read Shivon Zilis' full post"I feel happy that I got to show Elon how it feels to be deeply understood, nurtured, and peacefully loved with stability and gentleness. Given the tumultuous nature of his early life, his often tortured soul, and how hard he fights for humanity I wanted him to feel the deepest and most stable form of love this world can provide. My heart is full knowing I got to do that, and I hope it leaves a lasting good effect."We were always his safe space. A place where all of us were overjoyed to see him and one that was always full of happiness and love, not war, in contrast to his otherwise militant existence (a needed break from the battlefield where he could recharge his heart and soul before heading back out)"I loved being that counterbalancing place of safety, sense of calm, and love — and delighted in bringing a smile back to his face when he was down. I will miss him dearly."I’ve loved him more than life itself and he’s taught me 100 lifetimes of knowledge and made my cup overflow with life meaning, so there is a lot of loss, but luckily we created four beautiful little loves of my life ❤️❤️❤️❤️ I am so beyond grateful for our children and they make every single day the best day of my life! I do hope and pray he and I can be great friends and coparents.I’m hurting, but care deeply about E and will always be cheering for his happiness. God speed, Elon, the world is lucky to have you."Who is Shivon Zilis?Zilis is a Canadian AI executive, venture capitalist and a former board member of OpenAI. She graduated from Yale with degrees in economics and philosophy. She began her career with IBM in Peru and Indonesia. She later became a founding partner at Bloomberg Beta focusing on machine intelligence investments. Zilis joined Neuralink in 2017 and eventually became its director of operations and special projects. This put her in Musk's professional orbit on a much closer basis. articles.summary: Alex Murdaugh's defense claims prosecutors withheld a witness statement alleging a police chief handled the murder weapons after the 2021 killings.
articles.body: Attorneys for Alex Murdaugh accused prosecutors Wednesday of withholding a witness statement alleging a South Carolina police chief handled the weapons used to kill Murdaugh's wife and son and arranged a change of clothes for him after the 2021 killings. And they're asking a judge to intervene. Murdaugh was convicted in 2023 of murdering his wife, Maggie, and son, Paul, at the family's Moselle property in Colleton County. The South Carolina Supreme Court later overturned the convictions after finding that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced the jury. His retrial is scheduled to begin April 5, 2027. The motion, filed by Murdaugh's attorneys Wednesday, cites press reports that a state grand jury heard testimony alleging Yemassee Police Chief Greg Alexander was seen with the murder weapons shortly after the June 7, 2021, killings. ALEX MURDAUGH DEMANDS NEW EVIDENCE SEARCH IN HUNT FOR CRACKS IN CASE "According to those reports, witnesses have testified that the Chief of Police of the Town of Yemassee, Greg Alexander, was seen with the murder weapons in the immediate aftermath of the June 7, 2021, killings, and that second Yemassee officer is under investigation for transporting and concealing weapons and clothing," the filing states. It also cites a story from The Post and Courier, which reported that "a Lowcountry official told SLED agents that Chief Alexander 'spoke of arriving early to the murder scene and talked about providing a change of clothes to Murdaugh,' and that the official believed the guns and clothing were brought into the police station and stored there." articles.title: Christa Pike was on a ventilator and unconscious after failed Tennessee execution, attorneys say
articles.body:
Christa Pike was placed on a ventilator and unconscious in a hospital in the hours after her failed execution in Tennessee, her attorneys said in a court filing Friday.

Hospital staff, her lawyers said, were working to save Pike's life and clear the two doses of the drug that the state uses to execute prisoners.

The stunning failure in Tennessee's execution chamber on Wednesday has left both sides on the death penalty debate demanding answers. The state's governor has ordered an independent review.

In the court filing, Pike's attorneys said they believed problems with the IV lines caused the lethal drug pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.

"Apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms. Pike's body," they wrote.

Instead of "remedying this failure," they prepared and administered a backup set of pentobarbital syringe, her lawyers said.

State officials have not offered any explanation about what went wrong during the execution attempt

Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee demanded a review of the state's execution procedures and indefinitely postponed Pike's execution and another one slated for this year. Other Republican political leaders in Tennessee said the state should review whether to stop single-drug lethal injections and consider other options to carry out death sentences.

The execution team worked for an hour to administer the lethal drugs, said Pike's defense lawyer Randy Spivey, who counted at least seven needles in her left arm.

Neither the initial nor the backup dose of pentobarbital worked. Pike was still snoring when the execution chamber's microphone was cut off more than an hour into the attempt.

articles.summary: Nagpur garage fire in Teka Naka gutted 17 two-wheelers; owner alleges sacked mechanic set blaze. Losses estimated at Rs10 lakh; no casualties.
articles.body: Nagpur: A fire broke out at an automobile workshop in Bank Colony, Teka Naka, early Friday morning, gutting 17 two-wheelers kept at the garage for servicing, causing losses estimated at around Rs7 lakh. The workshop owner alleged that the fire was set by a sacked mechanic of the garage.The fire broke out at around 3.42am in the workshop on Nari Road. A fire tender from Sugat Nagar fire station reached the spot within minutes and firefighters brought the blaze under control by around 5.27am.Workshop owner Satish Yadav told reporters that he dismissed an employee around two months ago. Yadav alleged that the employee, who worked as a mechanic, had been removed from service over his alcohol addiction.Yadav alleged the employee set fire to the workshop. The flames rapidly spread through the premises, damaging vehicles kept for repairs and also affecting adjoining establishments.The fire brigade’s spot report recorded that 17 two-wheelers were damaged in the blaze. The fire also damaged a nearby clinic. The doctor said he received a call from Yadav around 3.30am informing him that his clinic had caught fire.The blaze also damaged portions of the building, including the roof and adjoining shops. The overall loss from the incident is estimated at around Rs10 lakh.Yadav said he had lodged a police complaint at Kapil Nagar police station. The alleged motive and exact cause of the fire are yet to be established. articles.title: 36 private vehicles used for deliveries seized in Ghaziabad
articles.summary: Ghaziabad transport dept seized 36 privately registered bikes used for Swiggy/Zomato/Blinkit deliveries, enforcing UP Group & Delivery Service Provider Rules 2026.
articles.body: Ghaziabad: The transport department has seized 36 privately registered motorcycles being used for commercial deliveries by aggregators and delivery platforms such as Swiggy, Zomato and Blinkit in the city.Under the new Uttar Pradesh Group and Delivery Service Provider Rules, 2026, notified by the state govt on May 22 this year, aggregators and delivery service providers are supposed to obtain a special licence for operating in the state. It can cover businesses involved in ride-hailing, food delivery, quick commerce and other hyperlocal deliveries where they operate on motor vehicles. It came into force 15 days after the notification.According to the rules, existing aggregators and delivery services have to obtain a licence, while new operators must obtain one before commencing operations. The licence will be issued by the State Transport Authority (STA) and will be valid for five years. The aggregators had to file an application online and pay a fee of Rs 25,000. They need to pay a licence fee of Rs 5 lakh and pay a security deposit depending on the fleet size.An enforcement drive was conducted on Thursday. Ghaziabad ARTO (enforcement) Amit Ranjan Rai said the new policy aims to bring aggregator and delivery service operations under a regulatory framework that prioritizes passenger safety, driver well-being, pollution reduction, encouragement of electric vehicles, fare transparency, and time-bound grievance resolution. “We are verifying vehicle documents and company records to ensure compliance with the applicable rules. Action has been taken against 36 vehicles found being used for commercial purposes despite being registered for private use,” he said.“During inspections, we found instances of privately registered vehicles being used for commercial activities including Blinkit, Zomato, Swiggy and the concerned aggregator companies had not obtained the requisite licence from the transport commissioner for fleet operations in Uttar Pradesh,” Rai told TOI. “We have also directed companies to fulfil the necessary licensing and registration formalities and submit details of vehicles operating under their networks.”TOI tried reaching out to the companies but they did not respond.The department has also asked vehicle owners to ensure that their vehicles are used only for purposes permitted under their registration.
